reason: The text contains the character Arnan (אָרְנָן הַיְבוּסִי - Arnan the Jebusite), who is explicitly named but portrayed as a regular person. He is not royal, not a prophet, and not a supernatural being. He is depicted as a property owner and farmer engaged in threshing wheat, who shows deference to King David and offers his resources. While other named characters in the passage include royalty (David), military commanders (Joab), prophets (Gad), and supernatural beings (Satan, God, the angel), Arnan is clearly characterized as an ordinary person of modest means.
